title: Multimodal Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution via Contrastive Evidence Reasoning
research_question: Can a training-free, zero-shot multimodal framework resolve cross-document event coreference competitively by contrasting explanations for same-event and different-event hypotheses while also supporting streaming updates?
methodology: The paper proposes MM-CDECR, which reframes pairwise event coreference as abductive inference rather than supervised discriminative matching. For each candidate pair, a multimodal large language model generates and compares explanations under competing same-event and different-event hypotheses using coherence, parsimony, and consistency. Multimodal fingerprinting is used for retrieval, and incremental graph clustering supports streaming updates. The framework is evaluated without task-specific training on ECB+, AIDA Phase 1, and WEC-Eng.

key_findings.finding: MM-CDECR reports CoNLL F1 scores of 88.1% on ECB+, 73.3% on AIDA Phase 1, and 72.2% on WEC-Eng.
On ECB+, the training-free framework reportedly matches the strongest supervised text-only system in aggregate CoNLL F1 and obtains the best B3 and CEAFe scores among non-oracle baselines.
On AIDA Phase 1, MM-CDECR reportedly exceeds the best prior multimodal-benchmark baseline by 6.6 points.
On WEC-Eng, MM-CDECR reportedly exceeds the best supervised baseline by 6.3 points.
The framework performs coreference inference without task-specific training data and produces abductive explanations for individual decisions.
Incremental graph clustering is explicitly part of the design, making the paper relevant to continuity when new event evidence arrives over time.

Generalization of the reported results to enterprise email or workplace chat work-matter identity is not established by the abstract, because the evaluations use event-coreference benchmarks rather than workplace communication corpora.

limitations: Only the abstract was accessible through the web source, so implementation details, ablations, error analysis, and author-stated limitations could not be verified.
The reported evaluation is on ECB+, AIDA Phase 1, and WEC-Eng rather than enterprise email or workplace chat.
The abstract does not establish whether incremental graph updates preserve identity correctly when an event changes substantially or when earlier identity decisions must be revised.
Dependence on multimodal large language models introduces model-specific behavior whose reproducibility cannot be assessed from the abstract.
No code or dedicated dataset release is identified in the accessible abstract.
raw_claims: Cross-document event coreference groups mentions from different documents that refer to one real-world event.
MM-CDECR treats coreference as a choice between competing explanatory hypotheses.
The method compares explanations for same-event and different-event interpretations.
The framework operates in a zero-shot multimodal setting.
Multimodal fingerprinting is used to retrieve candidate evidence efficiently.
Incremental graph clustering is used to update event structure as new information arrives.
The method is evaluated on ECB+, AIDA Phase 1, and WEC-Eng.
The reported CoNLL F1 values are 88.1%, 73.3%, and 72.2% on those three datasets respectively.
The authors report improvements over prior baselines on AIDA and WEC-Eng without task-specific training.
The system produces explanatory reasoning associated with its coreference decisions.
